individuals.treatment_summary: Colchicine, with significant improvement of symptoms (Table 2: colchicine, partial response); in remission at sample collection.
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Targeted NGS panel for autoinflammatory diseases revealed a heterozygous TNFAIP3 c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation, confirmed by Sanger sequencing; no mutation in 14 genes of autosomal recessive autoinflammatory diseases; phenotype compatible with HA20; reduced A20 in PBMCs.

variants.parental_testing_statement: Sanger sequencing identified the variation in the affected father (I.1) and sister (II.1); electropherograms show the heterozygous variation in II.2 but not in her healthy mother (I.2) (Figure 1A).
variants.functional_evidence_statement: A20 expression significantly reduced in this individual's PBMCs, as in all three patients (I.1, II.1, II.2) vs two healthy individuals (Figure 3A). In vitro (HEK293T): steady-state A20_Leu236Pro 47.6% of WT; half-life 2.8 hr vs WT still highly expressed at 24 hr; accumulation to 91.3% of WT with MG132 (enhanced proteasomal degradation, also by flow cytometry); reduced inhibition of TNFα-induced NF-κB activity; decreased deubiquitination of TRAF6. In silico: PremPS ΔΔG 1.820 kcal/mol (destabilizing); CADD 29.5; absent from gnomAD; Leu236 invariant across species.
